statement.p: Calculate the Taylor polynomials T_2(x) and T_3(x) centered at x = \pi for f(x) = \cos\mathopen{}\left(x\right).

static.solution:
\begin{array}{lcll} T(x) \amp = \amp \amp f(a) \cr\cr \amp \amp + \amp \frac{f'(a)}{1!} (x-a) \cr \cr \amp \amp + \amp \frac{f''(a)}{2!} (x-a)^2 \cr \cr \amp \amp + \amp \ldots \cr \cr \amp \amp + \amp \frac{f^n(a)}{n!} (x-a)^n \end{array}
So, in this case, f(x) = \cos\mathopen{}\left(x\right) and
T_2(x) = A + B(x-\pi ) + C(x-\pi )^2
where
A=f(\pi )=-1=-1
B=f'(\pi )=0=0
C=\frac{f''(\pi )}{2!}=\frac{1}{2}=0.5
Thus,
T_2(x) = -1 + 0 (x - \pi ) + \frac{1}{2} (x - \pi )^2
or
T_2(x) = 0.5\mathopen{}\left(x-\pi \right)^{2}-1
Similarly,
T_3(x) = D + E(x-\pi ) + F(x-\pi )^2 + G(x-\pi )^3
where
D=f(\pi )=-1 = -1
E=f'(\pi )=0 =0
F=\frac{f''(\pi )}{2!}=\frac{1}{2} =0.5
G=\frac{f'''(\pi )}{3!}=0=0
Thus, T_3(x) = -1 + 0 (x - \pi ) + \frac{1}{2} (x - \pi )^2 + 0 (x - \pi )^3
or
T_3(x) = 0.5\mathopen{}\left(x-\pi \right)^{2}-1
